dimensions.assessment: Affects children, teens, parents, and all public-facing artificial intelligence chatbot providers operating in the United States.
dimensions.evidence: To require the creation of family accounts for children to be able to use artificial intelligence chatbots, to require verifiable parental consent for teens using artificial intelligence chatbots, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Requires major operational, verification, parental control, and data handling modifications for chatbot platforms and terminates non-compliant existing accounts.
dimensions.evidence: A covered entity shall terminate any user account or profile of an artificial intelligence chatbot of the covered entity that exists as of the effective date of this Act if the covered entity knows such user is a child... or a teen

dimensions.assessment: Tasks federal bodies like the FTC and NSF with enforcement, studies, and reporting, but specifies no direct funding amounts.
dimensions.evidence: The Commission shall enforce this Act in the same manner... Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director of the National Science Foundation shall conduct or commission a study

dimensions.assessment: Creates a comprehensive regulatory framework imposing new compliance duties, parental tools, advertising restrictions, and enforcement mechanisms via the FTC and state attorneys general.
dimensions.evidence: A violation of this Act shall be treated as a violation of a rule defining an unfair or deceptive act or practice prescribed under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent regulatory standards taking effect one year after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This Act shall take effect on the date that is 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act.

importance_detail.rationale: This bill establishes federal requirements for AI chatbot providers regarding family accounts for children, verifiable parental consent for teens, parental controls, data deletion, targeted advertising prohibitions, and federal/state enforcement.

label: S. 4407

latest_action.text: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The S. 4407 - CHATBOT Act establishes specific requirements for public-facing websites, online services, and software applications that provide artificial intelligence chatbots to users, focusing particularly on child and teen safety. The bill requires family accounts managed by parents for children under 13, verifiable parental consent for teens aged 13 through 17, and specific default privacy protections and parental control settings. It also bans targeted advertising using the personal data of children and teens, provides for enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, and mandates studies and reports on the impacts of AI chatbots on minors.

affected_groups.effect: Must use artificial intelligence chatbots through a family account managed by a parent, and existing standalone accounts without a family account are terminated with personal data deleted.
Must have direct parental notice and verifiable parental consent provided by a parent to maintain or create an account, or have a family account established.
Granted options to create family accounts, provide or revoke consent, set parental controls like time limits and notification blocks, and access chat logs and activity records.

Must implement family accounts, parental consent mechanisms, default protective settings, transparency labels, delete personal data upon account termination, and refrain from targeted advertising to minors.

key_provisions: Requires covered entities to mandate family accounts for child users under 13 and terminate existing child and teen accounts unless parental consent or family accounts are established.
Requires covered entities to provide direct notice to parents and obtain verifiable parental consent before teens aged 13 to 17 can create user accounts or profiles.
Mandates specific parental controls within family accounts, including time limits, disabling rewards or financial transactions, turning off push notifications, and transparency label settings.
Prohibits covered entities from using personal data collected from children and teens for targeted advertising.
Directs the National Science Foundation to study the effects of artificial intelligence chatbots on human relationships and the social needs of children and teens.
Requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to submit a report examining the effectiveness of the Act, adoption rates, compliance, and recommendations for improvement.
missing_information: Specific civil penalty dollar amounts for violations of the Act are not detailed in the text, as enforcement relies on incorporating the provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Exact technical methods acceptable for obtaining verifiable parental consent are not explicitly prescribed beyond referencing compliance standards under the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998.

The bill requires family accounts managed by parents for children under 13, verifiable parental consent for teens aged 13 through 17, and specific default privacy protections and parental control settings. summary_detail.significance: The legislation establishes new regulatory oversight over artificial intelligence chatbot providers regarding minor users, impacting how companies handle account creation, parental consent, data retention, and targeted advertising for children and teens nationwide.
